definition: A voter asked for a mail ballot (or is on a permanent mail list).
The election office mailed the ballot. In all-mail states every registered voter is sent one.
The ballot envelope came back to the election office. Not yet checked.
The envelope passed signature or ID checks and the ballot will be counted.
The ballot has been run through a tabulator. Results are released after polls close.
Votes cast at an early voting site before Election Day.
The source printed a specific count.
The source printed a rounded figure ("about 320,000"). Shown with ≈ and never added to exact counts.
A model or provider estimate, such as AP's expected vote. Always labeled with its provider.
No figure has been published or could be read. Left blank, never filled in.
Published by a state or county election office (directly, or quoted by news from that office).
Compiled by a third party from official files. Timing and definitions can differ from the state's own.
The date or time the figure describes.
When the refresh last tried the source. "No change" and "could not retrieve" are logged separately.
The increase since the previous report from the same source. Not the same as ballots cast that day.
Cook Political Report ratings, from most to least competitive. They are expert judgments, not probabilities.
The rater favors the party that does not hold the seat now.
Ahead in counted votes; called by a named news organization; official after canvass.
